I'd like to hear from payments operations and liquidity risk on their confirmed requirements covering liquidity, collateral, and monitoring. Please walk me through what you've confirmed so we can record those inputs in the plan. If there are any unresolved funding gaps, we can flag those for escalation after this meeting rather than holding up the sign-off decision.

transcript.text: Thank you both for those confirmations. Let me summarize what we have on the record so far. Jonas, you've confirmed a modeled peak two-hour net settlement outflow of $6,500,000. Elena, you've confirmed $4,000,000 in unencumbered Treasury bills eligible for the rail's liquidity facility, with a daily eligibility and substitution check required under our liquidity-risk policy. Before I make my sign-off decision, I'd like to hear from payments operations on the monitoring requirements — specifically what real-time or near-real-time monitoring controls are in place for instant-payment flows, settlement positions, and intraday liquidity. And Elena, if you can confirm the daily eligibility check as the monitoring cadence for collateral, that would round out the monitoring section of the operating plan. Once I have the monitoring confirmation, I'm prepared to proceed with the sign-off decision and flag the $2.5 million gap for escalation as we discussed.

transcript.text: Thanks, Maya. On the monitoring side, here's what payments operations has confirmed. For real-time monitoring of instant-payment flows, we'll have a dashboard tracking inbound and outbound payment volumes and values on the rail, with position updates every 60 seconds. For settlement positions, we'll monitor our net settlement position continuously during rail operating hours, with alerts triggered if our net outflow exceeds 70% of the modeled peak — so at approximately $4.55 million — to give us early warning before we approach the $6.5 million peak. For intraday liquidity, we'll track available collateral and settlement funding on an hourly basis, aligned with Elena's daily eligibility check on the collateral side. I should note that these monitoring controls are documented in our operations runbook for the rail, and I can confirm them here for the operating plan. The runbook itself hasn't been formally attached to the plan file yet, but the controls are confirmed and ready to be recorded.
